supporting_observations.claim: WS-LMARTINS-01 (10.40.10.22) made eight recorded TCP connections to the explicit proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080 between 13:35:56 and 14:05:48 UTC. Zeek classified these connections as HTTP.

The recorded proxy connections recur approximately every five minutes, with successive intervals of approximately 4.3–5.5 minutes. This supports periodic network activity but does not identify its purpose.

The available records for the periodic connections contain connection metadata and byte counts, but no originating executable or ultimate external destination. They therefore do not distinguish approved updater traffic from malicious beaconing.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied periodic-flow records terminate at the internal proxy; they do not include proxy CONNECT targets, URLs, external IP addresses, TLS SNI, or certificates establishing the alerted outbound HTTPS destinations (T036-00101, T036-00144, T036-00178, T036-00208, T036-00235, T036-00242, T036-00256).

No process attribution accompanies these periodic-flow records, preventing correlation to pfupdater.exe or another executable (T036-00101, T036-00144, T036-00178, T036-00208, T036-00235, T036-00242, T036-00256).
claims_not_established: Whether the periodic connections reached updates.pixelforge-suite.com and originated from the approved PixelForge updater; cadence alone does not establish that attribution (T036-00101, T036-00144, T036-00178, T036-00208, T036-00235, T036-00242, T036-00256).

Whether these connections carried command-and-control traffic, exfiltrated data, or performed benign update checks; the supplied connection metadata does not establish application content or intent (T036-00144, T036-00178, T036-00208, T036-00256).
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve PROXY-NWD-01 access and CONNECT logs for 10.40.10.22 during 13:20–14:20 UTC, including target hostnames, ports, timestamps, and transaction identifiers; correlate them with the recorded source ports.
Retrieve endpoint network telemetry linking the periodic proxy connections to process IDs, executable paths, command lines, parent processes, hashes, and signatures.
Correlate resolved destinations and process identity with the approved PixelForge service and updater. Obtain updater logs or relevant TLS/application metadata if attribution remains unresolved.
